description: rebaseWhen is set explicitly because the default 'auto' only rebases behind-base branches when automerge is on.

packageRules.description: pixi bumps move the three workflow pixi-version pins and constraints.pixi together on one Renovate branch (same depName+datasource+currentValue). Automerge is on: every step is lock-format safe (newer pixi reads older locks), and a contributor on stale pixi gets pixi's native self-update message. See experiments/claude/design_specs/2026-08-02-renovate-pixi-workflow-version.md.
gwaslab pins adjusttext >=0.7.3,<=0.8, so adjusttext 1.x can never resolve and pixi lock fails. Lift this ceiling only once gwaslab relaxes its pin.

setuptools 82 removed pkg_resources, which zepid still imports at import time. See the comment above the setuptools pin in pyproject.toml. Lift this ceiling only once zepid no longer imports pkg_resources.
r-base>=4.6 seems currently incompatible with r-cpp11
upload pages v4 introduced a gotcha and potentially breaking change

The Docker datasource returns no releaseTimestamp for tag lists, and the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour of timestamp-required marks a timestamp-less release pending forever rather than for minimumReleaseAge. That silently pinned the renovate image at 44.5.3 with the 44.30.3 bump parked in Pending Status Checks. Scoped to the datasource rather than one package so a future Docker dep does not hit the same trap, and left at the fail-closed default elsewhere: conda, PyPI and github-releases all do return timestamps, so they keep the real soak.

lockFileMaintenance.description: minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour is relaxed because a lockFileMaintenance upgrade is not a release: it has no version and no releaseTimestamp, so the repo-level minimumReleaseAge combined with the default timestamp-required pinned stabilityStatus to yellow on every run. That left renovate/stability-days permanently pending and, since platformAutomerge is off, blocked Renovate's own automerge forever rather than for one day. The soak never applied to lock refreshes anyway -- pixi lock resolves against whatever is newest within the pyproject.toml ranges, which minimumReleaseAge does not constrain.
